claim: Models are mapped under bin/archive/pokemon for Sword/Shield.
Pokemon models use .gfbmdl and are commonly stored in .gfpak archives.
Pokemon textures are stored in .gfpak resources; documented texture containers include BNTX.
Maintained exporter identifies GFBANM as the animation family used by Let's Go and Sword/Shield.
Official in-game battle screenshots are suitable for battle-camera/appearance cross-checking but not raw-asset equivalence.
68x56 Gen VIII Pokemon box icons are a UI asset track and must not be treated as canonical battle sprites.
BDSP reconstruction targets Unity 2019.4.27f1 and reconstructs resources through Unity/AssetRipper workflows.
Pokemon resources are separated across common/battle/field bundles; common contains model/main animations/textures and battle contains battle rig/scripts and battle-exclusive animations.
Bundle naming documents form/gender distinctions and normal versus shiny texture variants.
Official battle captures can validate appearance/camera but are not raw model sources.
Pokemon archive folder maps to bin/archive/pokemon; pokemon_info_list.bin and poke_resource_table.trpmcatalog are identified resource metadata.
Maintained tooling supports TRMDL-family models and distinguishes _rare.trmtr material loading for rare/shiny appearance.
Maintained exporter identifies TRANM as the animation family used by Legends: Arceus and later titles.
Older PLA-specific Blender importer and prepared model-dump workflow provide a preservation cross-check, not automatic Tier-A provenance.
Final acceptance requires 64x64 PNG plus source image, target palette, 4bpp, compressed binary, manifests, full SHA-256 chain, dedup, validation and reproducible scripts.
